items.md: 6. Petitioners after amendment of *Warabandi* started irrigating their land. It was pointed out that appeal was filed on 18.06.2009, whereas note on said page of the appeal evidences to the fact that status quo granted and the date below mentioned is 17.06.2009. Canal water was sanctioned in favour of the petitioners but in the memorandum of appeal only petitioners No.1 to 3 have been impleaded as party whereas petitioners No.4 and 5 have been left out, this material aspect while deciding the appeal was ignored by respondent No.2. Petitioners purchased their land and share of each petitioner is mentioned in Register Haqdaran-e-Zamin, therefore, canal water was accordingly sanctioned separately by respondent No.1. Single appeal without impleading petitioners No. 4 & 5 was not competent, the order passed by respondent No.1 was set aside completely, which was unwarranted in law. It was contended that respondent No.2 in impugned order reasoned that the land was allotted under the Tube-Well Sinking Scheme, so without obtaining NOC from the District Collector no canal water could be sanctioned, this was factually incorrect as land was not the ownership of the Provincial Government but petitioners are vendees/purchasers.

items.md: Right of ownership even under section 30 of the Colonization of Government Land Act 1912, stands transferred in favour of the petitioners. Thus there was no need to obtain NOC before filing application for sanction of canal water. There is no bar for sanction of canal water in favour of the vendees who purchased property after grant of proprietary rights from original allottees. Respondent No.2 erred in law by giving such a finding. Moreover, quite a few persons enjoying the same status have been sanctioned canal water. According to KHAKA DASTI watercourse which irrigates land of different owners included in C.C.A including that of the respondents passes through the land of petitioners and the sanctioned NAKKA is also situated in the land of the petitioners. Report by Ziladar that petitioners have no other source of irrigation is also material. This important aspect was not examined by respondent No.2. The order passed by respondent No.2 is patently unlawful and unwarranted in law.

Rule 82 of the Rules under the Canal And Drainage Act, 1873 provide a period of thirty days for presenting an appeal, in its explanation it is provided that appeal may be admitted, even after the prescribed period if the appellant satisfies the court that he had fresh cause in respect of filing of appeal within the given period, therefore, the appeal filed was competent which was filed strictly within the meaning of section 84 of the Rules ibid. Respondent No.2 had powers to summarily reject the appeal if found unnecessary under section 85 of the Rules ibid.

10. Section 20 is attracted when a person not already enjoying water supply requires canal water for his land and such supply is to be conveyed through already existing watercourse, or when any person obtained land in which water is not previously sanctioned and he wants to get it included in the warabandi of any outlet. But if land already stands included in the Chakbandi and CCA of any outlet the owner of such land can get his land included in the warabandi under section 68. Because the water of such land is already flowing in the watercourse, therefore, section 20 is attracted only for a fresh supply for any other land which is not already in C.C.A.. or is not in Chakbandi of such outlet.

11. Section 20 further applies when site of any outlet is required to be changed, perhaps comes in the purview of words, "change of source of irrigation". If site of outlet is changed under section 20, distribution of water among the shareholders of such changed outlet will be done under section 68. The original jurisdiction entertaining any application

items.md: under section 68 lies with SDCO and Divisional Canal Officer possess the appellate power. The order of SDCO and DCO under section 68 is challengeable in the Civil Court if these are against provisions of section 68 or some other irregularities pertaining to jurisdiction appear therein. No such discrepancy is found in the present case. Petitioners land being already included in the Chakbandi and CCA, water of such land was already flowing in the watercourse, therefore, the application was rightly filed under section 68 of the Act ibid.

13. There is no denying the fact that the order was passed by respondent No.1 on 29.10.2008 which was assailed by the respondents on 18.06.2009. Respondent No.2 in his order failed to address the basic question raised by the petitioners with regard to question of limitation. The appeal filed before respondent No.2 was patently barred by time. Even under Rule 82 of the Rules under Canal & Drainage Act, 1873, it is expressly provided that any appeal admitted after prescribed period of thirty days as given in the said rule, appellant has to satisfy the Court that he had sufficient cause for not presenting the appeal within such period. Respondent No.2 in his order dated 21.07.2009 failed to address this basic question of law.
